correctness.rationale: For t>=1, E_(t-1) and E_(t+1) are disjoint, and every vertex of E_t has >=theta neighbors in the former, leaving <=Delta-theta in the latter; counting E_t--E_(t+1) edges both ways proves contraction. E0 disjoint E1 gives first-step bound. Layer construction has exact theta backwards and <=b forwards per vertex, yielding a front with extinction at h+2 and total size Theta((theta/b)^h); finite checker independently reproduced sample cases. No infinite conclusion is based on finite tests.

value.rationale: A dimensionless contact threshold above Delta/2 yields a universal geometric extinction mechanism and optimal logarithmic worst-case time on every finite graph with maximum degree <=Delta. It quantitatively strengthens the previously published general linear event budget by establishing the sharp leading constant, with an explicit natural layered family realizing it; the exact clock is useful to transient-mixing and excitation propagation questions.
